title: Existence and isomorphism theorem for pinned split realizations
statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative ring. Use finite reduced based root data and pinned split realizations over $A$ as defined in [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]. Every finite reduced based root datum $\mathcal R$ has a pinned split realization over $A$. If $P$ and $P'$ are pinned split realizations over $A$ of based data $\mathcal R$ and $\mathcal R'$, respectively, then each specified based-datum isomorphism $u:\mathcal R\simeq\mathcal R'$ is induced by a unique pinning-compatible $A$-group-scheme isomorphism $P\simeq P'$. This isomorphism induces the specified constant lattice map on the tori, even when $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is disconnected. There is no Noetherian, field, semisimplicity or positive-rank hypothesis.

source.place: Theorem 6.1.16(2), printed p.196, and Theorem 6.1.17 (Isomorphism Theorem), p.197; pinnings as in Definition 6.1.1, p.186 Read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Forget the base of $\mathcal R$ and realize its underlying reduced datum over $\mathbf Q$ by [lem-sfb-rational-split-root-realization]. Apply [lem-sfb-rational-split-integral-prolongation] to this particular split rational group and its specified torus to obtain a split realization $(\mathcal G,\mathcal T=D_{\mathbf Z}(M))$ over $\mathbf Z$ of the same datum. This input explicitly includes the full tangent decomposition and free rank-one integral root modules. Keep the original base $\Delta$ and choose a generator of each of its finitely many free root modules. This gives a pinning over $\mathbf Z$ by [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization], with no choice needed when $\Delta$ is empty. Now apply [lem-sfb-pinned-split-root-base-change] along $\mathbf Z\to A$ to obtain the desired pinned realization over $A$. No relation between $A$ and $\mathbf Q$ is required: only the integral model is pulled back.

source.place: Proposition 6.2.12, pp.211--212; Section 6.3, pp.212--229; Theorem 6.1.17, p.197; Definition 6.1.1, p.186

proof.text: For given $P,P'$ and $u$, write $h:M'\to M$ for the pullback on character lattices corresponding to $u$, and $b:\Phi\to\Phi'$ for the associated root bijection, so $h(b(\alpha))=\alpha$. The dual equality is exactly preservation of coroots. Apply [lem-sfb-split-central-isogeny-lifting] to the underlying split realizations. Since $h$ is an isomorphism, it gives an isomorphism $f:G\to G'$ with torus restriction exactly $D_A(h)$. For each simple root $\alpha$, its tangent map is an isomorphism between free rank-one root modules; hence there is a unique unit $a_{b(\alpha)}\in A^\times$ with $df(X_\alpha)=a_{b(\alpha)}X'_{b(\alpha)}$. Indeed, in the specified generators the map and its inverse are scalar multiplication by mutually inverse elements of $A$.

Put $Q'=\mathbf Z\Phi'$. The base axioms imply $Q'=\bigoplus_{\beta\in\Delta'}\mathbf Z\beta$: spanning follows from the integer simple-root expressions, and independence follows from their rational independence. Define $t:Q'\to A^\times$ by $t(\sum n_\beta\beta)=\prod a_\beta^{-n_\beta}$. By [lem-sfb-adjoint-torus-root-coordinates], this is an $A$-point of $T'/Z(G')$ acting by an automorphism $c_t$ which fixes $T'$ pointwise and scales its $\beta$-root line by $a_\beta^{-1}$. Therefore $F=c_t\circ f$ satisfies $dF(X_\alpha)=a_{b(\alpha)}^{-1}a_{b(\alpha)}X'_{b(\alpha)}=X'_{b(\alpha)}$. Its torus map is still exactly $D_A(h)$, so it induces the specified based isomorphism and respects the pinning.

source.place: Proof of Corollary 6.1.15, p.196 (simple-root coordinates); deduction of Theorem 6.1.17, p.197

proof.text: If $F_1,F_2$ are two pinning-compatible isomorphisms inducing $u$, their torus restrictions are both $D_A(h)$ by definition. By [lem-sfb-split-central-isogeny-lifting], $F_2=c_t\circ F_1$ for a unique $t\in(T'/Z(G'))(A)$. By [lem-sfb-adjoint-torus-root-coordinates] and the equality of the pinned generators, $t(\beta)X'_\beta=X'_\beta$ for every $\beta\in\Delta'$, so $t(\beta)=1$. The basis description in step 3 forces $t=1$, whence $F_1=F_2$. This uses units of the full ring $A$ and the specified constant lattice map, without decomposing its spectrum into connected components. With empty roots $Q'=0$, the same argument has an empty product and a trivial adjoint torus.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q156-b235ee4eb (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all four new nodes, the cited definition, diagonalizable-group and base-change nodes, and the duplicate candidates (integral-root-datum-isogenies with its full proof, root-datum-realization, root-datum-isogeny-realization, isogeny-simple-root-rigidity, relative-reductive-centre-weight-kernel, chevalley-integral-root-model, relative-central-multiplicative-quotient, among others). Conrad is not in literature/, so I fetched the public PDF and read it with pdftotext: Def 6.1.1, Cor 6.1.15 and its proof (pp.195-196), Thm 6.1.16(1),(2) (p.196), Thm 6.1.17 with its deduction 'from 6.1.16 and the Z-basis Δ of X(T/Z_G) in the proof of 6.1.15' (p.197), Prop 6.2.12 (pp.211-212), Lemma 6.3.1 and the end of §6.3, Cor 3.3.6(1) and Ex 5.1.7. The split follows this route exactly. Step 1: realization over Q, then the integral prolongation of that same Q-group, then a choice of pinning over Z, then base change along Z→A (the base-change node allows any ring map). Step 2: I checked directions with h=u^{-1}, b=u: h(bα)=α and h^∨(α^∨)=(uα)^∨, so the isogeny node gives an isomorphism with torus map D_A(u^{-1}), and its root-line maps are units. Step 3: Δ' is a Z-basis of ZΦ', t(β)=a_β^{-1} lies in D_A(Q')=T'/Z, and c_t fixes T' while correcting the root-line scalars. Step 4: t(β)=1 on Δ', so t=1; this is a ring identity, valid on disconnected and nonreduced spectra. All new nodes are true. I tested the isogeny node on SL2→PGL2 (kernel μ_2, not smooth over F_2). Its clause on every homomorphism with the given torus restriction holds, because the rank-one relation forces c_α c_{-α}=1. No node duplicates an existing one: the existing nodes work over algebraically closed fields, need a Noetherian base, or would make a cycle. The isogeny half of integral-root-datum-isogenies is now a specialisation of the new isogeny node; this is a note for the maintainer, not a fault. No single new node states either clause of the item. Warning for later splits: the proofs of the rational-realization and prolongation nodes need the isomorphism theorem over a field and must cite the isogeny and adjoint-torus nodes, not the item, to avoid a cycle. Batch 5: every flagged path runs through the general definition def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization, which was already a statement dependency of the item, to the Mathlib leaf lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent. That leaf is generic fpqc descent of smoothness, not the trace formula or Poincaré duality. Every node is in unit sk-thm-sf-ctf-stability, so there are no tool_uses. No changes.
